doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Bucky's kids and the characters who visited the house
summary: His son John's trio, and how the children met Zoot Sims, Joe Venuti and Slam Stewart at home.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Your kids have done well for themselves. I’m wondering if you’ve gotten to the point where you learn anything from them?

Oh yeah. Yeah. They come up with some good stuff. Tunes — I know John is about to make an album. He does a lot of research on it. I used to tell him listen to this guy, listen to that guy. He does a great rendition of a certain tune you ought to look into. That’s all. That’s as far as it goes. But he’s got a hot trio. They’re very good.
Yeah. He’s got a good personality on stage.
Yeah. Well he works at it.
When they were kids did they have a sense that what you did was a little bit different than what other people’s fathers did?
Oh they know that. They know that. They know what I did. When he hears an old record he says, “That’s you playing” he says, “I can tell you a mile away.”

Yeah. He can. And Zoot Sims used to come over a lot so they met all the characters. Even Benny you know, or Joe Venuti. Slam Stewart lived at the house for a while and we did gigs together so they got a good cross section of what happened 20 years before they did.

And they remember every line, every joke. John even taped something of Joe Venuti telling a story and it’s priceless. But I’m glad they got that education from the big guns like that, especially Zoot, Zoot Sims.
